facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Net leverage rose from 0.33x at the 2023 year end to 1.71x at the 2025 year end because the company turned cash into inventory, not because earnings fell: real estate grew from USD 1,790.3 million to USD 2,645.1 million while cash fell from USD 616.0 million to USD 379.2 million, fiscal 2025 added a net USD 100.0 million of debt, and EBITDA was USD 237.8 million in fiscal 2023 and USD 247.2 million in fiscal 2025. By June 30, 2026 net leverage had eased to 1.57x as inventory growth slowed: cash put into real estate was USD 69.3 million in the nine months against USD 561.0 million a year earlier. Leverage here is therefore set by how fast the company invests in land, which management controls, and it will rise again if the fiscal 2025 pace of investment returns without matching earnings growth. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: EBITDA was USD 237.8 million in fiscal 2023, USD 281.4 million in fiscal 2024 and USD 247.2 million in fiscal 2025. The fiscal 2025 fall came from selling, general and administrative expense rising from USD 118.5 million to USD 154.4 million and from gross margin slipping from 23.80% to 21.87%, only partly offset by revenue growth to USD 1,662.4 million. In the nine months to June 30, 2026 revenue rose 6.29% on tract and other land sales of USD 90.4 million against USD 14.6 million, while residential lot sales revenue slipped from USD 977.3 million to USD 963.9 million and gross margin eased to 20.80%; EBITDA grew only from USD 121.2 million to USD 127.7 million. The earnings base that supports the debt has not recovered to the fiscal 2024 level, and the land sales that drive growth are lumpy. Basis: calculation K01; calculation K13; calculation K14; calculation K25; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Cash interest cover cannot be calculated: the cash flow statements print no interest paid, and all interest incurred is capitalized to real estate and released to cost of sales as lots are sold. Interest incurred rose from USD 32.6 million in fiscal 2024 to USD 45.5 million in fiscal 2025 after the 6.5% 2033 notes replaced the 3.85% 2026 notes. On that accrual proxy EBITDA cover fell from 8.63x to 5.43x and is 5.01x for the twelve months to June 30, 2026; the two notes alone carry USD 47.5 million of annual coupons, which twelve-month EBITDA covers 5.34x. The cash figure may differ because coupons are paid semiannually: accrued interest was USD 14.4 million at June 30, 2026 against USD 2.5 million at September 30, 2025. Cover stays at or above 5.01x on these proxies, but the direction since fiscal 2024 is down and no cash evidence confirms the level. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Operating cash flow was USD 364.1 million in fiscal 2023, when real estate fell by USD 206.3 million, then an outflow of USD 158.4 million in fiscal 2024 and USD 197.7 million in fiscal 2025 as real estate grew. facts.text: Several claims sit outside the debt figure. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against caution is the issuer's own measure: net debt to total capital was 17.7% at June 30, 2026 against a stated long-term aim of approximately 40% or less, no covenant breach is reported, and contracted lot sales to the controlling shareholder have a remaining sales price of USD 2,095.1 million against earnest money of USD 195.3 million. The cautious reading would fall away if covenant levels and the borrowing base proved wide, if cash interest paid matched the accrual proxy, and if operating cash flow stayed positive through the fiscal fourth quarter. It would harden if the annual report for fiscal 2026 showed operating outflows of the fiscal 2025 size with EBITDA below USD 247.2 million, or if the October 28, 2026 revolver tranche lapsed without replacement. Basis: calculation K16; calculation K24; calculation K11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 23

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Control sits with one industrial parent, and no parent guarantee or support for the Company's debt is stated. D.R. Horton owns about 62% of the common stock, designates four of seven directors and the Executive Chairman, and while it holds at least 35% must consent to new equity classes, executive changes, certain acquisitions and debt that takes total leverage above 40%. The consent right limits releveraging by the Company alone, but it also gives the parent a veto over refinancing choices; the filings do not define total leverage for this test, so it is not established as a creditor protection. Basis: calculation B10; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Revenue is concentrated in the controlling shareholder, so the Company's cash flow is a function of one buyer's demand. D.R. Horton accounted for 82.79% of residential lot sales revenues in fiscal 2025 and 85.97% in the nine months to June 30, 2026, against 82.89% a year earlier, and 80.61% of total revenues once tract sales are counted. Lot bankers that expect to resell to D.R. Horton add indirect dependence: USD 83.4 million of lots in fiscal 2025 and USD 33.4 million in the nine months. Contract strength partly offsets this, with USD 2,095.1 million of remaining sales price on owned lots under contract to the parent and USD 195.3 million of earnest money, 9.32% of that price. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The supply relationship is long but not binding on the parent. The Master Supply Agreement runs until June 29, 2037 or until D.R. Horton falls below 15% of voting shares, and the parent holds a right of first offer on lots, not an obligation to buy; it is not required to present land opportunities and is not restricted from competing, and lot sales contracts require an earnest money deposit that the Company may retain or refund on cancellation depending on the contract. The deposit is a modest share of the remaining price, so contracted revenue rests on the parent's willingness to close as much as on the deposit. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence for a lower risk view is behavioural and contractual: the Company has paid no dividend, the parent's leverage consent right works as a cap on debt, and its lot contracts carry USD 2,095.1 million of remaining sales price backed by USD 195.3 million of earnest money under a supply agreement that runs to 2037. The view would improve if the executed agreements showed firm purchase obligations and a defined leverage test, if the derivative suit were dismissed, and if the parent's own credit quality were shown to be strong. It would worsen if D.R. Horton fell below 35%, which ends its consent rights, or below 20%, which ends its board designation rights, if lot prices to the parent were reset, if its lot purchases fell, or if the Company paid a dividend or a related-party payment out of debt-funded cash. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Dependence on one controlling customer is the dominant credit risk, because that customer sets both the volume and the price of most revenue. D.R. Horton owns about 62% of the common stock, bought 82.79% of residential lot sales revenues in fiscal 2025 and 85.97% in the nine months to June 30, 2026 (82.89% a year earlier), and has USD 2,095.1 million of remaining sales price under contract with earnest money of only 9.32% of it. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence for a better view is that the balance sheet improved in the same season: net debt to total capital was 17.7% at June 30, 2026 against 28.9% a year earlier, operating cash flow turned positive with no borrowing on the revolver, no dividend has been paid and the parent holds USD 2,095.1 million of contracted remaining sales price. If fiscal 2026 shows positive operating cash flow for the full year, EBITDA at or above USD 253.7 million and a replacement for the revolver tranche, the view would move toward strong on liquidity and leverage. The strongest evidence for a worse view is concentration: the parent's share of lot revenues rose from 82.89% to 85.97% between the two nine-month periods while lots sold fell 8.64%, and no purchase obligation exists. The view would weaken if that share passed the fiscal 2024 level of 87.30% while volumes fell, if net cash put into real estate returned to the nine-month 2025 pace of USD 561.0 million with EBITDA below USD 247.2 million, which would put net debt above 1.71x EBITDA, or if the parent's holding fell below 35%. facts.label: Outlook
facts.text: Over the next 12 to 24 months management describes demand as held back by affordability and cautious consumer sentiment with elevated builder incentives, yet third-quarter revenues rose 4.23% and net cash put into real estate has been cut; the sector headwind is elevated mortgage rates and the company headwind is lower lot volume at higher prices. The notes due March 1, 2028 fall inside this window, about 15 months after the as-of date, and the 2028 notes became redeemable at par after March 1, 2026, so refinancing can begin early; the outcome of the revolver tranche scheduled for October 28, 2026 and the results for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026 are not established. The implication for revenue and margin is pressure; for liquidity and refinancing it is stability, with deleveraging dependent on land spending staying low. The implication for revenue and margin is pressure; for liquidity and refinancing it is stability, with deleveraging dependent on land spending staying low.

facts.text: The downside path starts with mortgage rates staying elevated and builder demand softening further, so D.R. Horton slows takedowns of the lots it has under contract and seeks lower prices. The first operational break is closings moving beyond the usual three to eighteen months, with earnest money of 9.32% of remaining sales price the only stated protection and the company free to retain or refund it on cancellation depending on the contract, while development spending on projects already started continues. Revenue and gross profit fall against overhead of USD 154.4 million in fiscal 2025, operating cash flow turns negative as it did in fiscal 2024 and 2025 even when revenue grew, and inventory rises. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: On the sensitivities in the calculations, a 25% fall in EBITDA to USD 190.3 million would put total debt at 4.17x and net debt at 2.10x, and if a fiscal 2025-sized free cash outflow of USD 199.9 million recurred, net debt would reach USD 598.8 million, 3.15x the reduced EBITDA and 24.39% of total capital, still well below the issuer's 40% aim. Liquidity of USD 1,064.8 million would still cover the notes due March 2028 3.55x, and the borrowing base, which is set on real estate book value and unrestricted cash, and the unquantified covenants are the unknowns. Management has levers: cut land and development spending, as it did by USD 491.7 million, walk away from land purchase contracts with deposits of USD 33.7 million against USD 615.9 million of remaining price, trim overhead, sell tract land and use the equity program with USD 300.0 million reserved. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress before March 2028, but leverage would rise sharply and refinancing would be at a higher cost, so the scenario weakens the credit without breaking it. The observable triggers are listed in the monitoring register. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Forestar presents an adequate business profile supported by modest leverage, USD 1,064.8 million of liquidity and contracted lots with its controlling shareholder, but credit quality is constrained by dependence on that shareholder for most revenue and by cash flow that follows inventory spending. Cash-flow durability appears adequate: EBITDA has stayed between USD 237.8 million and USD 281.4 million across three fiscal years and land spending is discretionary, but free cash flow was close to nil over those years. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on market access for the USD 300.0 million of notes due March 2028, the parent's continued purchases, and the borrowing base and covenants on the revolver. The primary downside path is a slower parent taking fewer lots at lower prices while development spending continues, which turns operating cash flow negative and raises net leverage. Further analysis would require cash interest paid, covenant levels and compliance certificates, the executed agreements with D.R. Horton, price by customer, results for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026 and peer data. Top risk: dependence on D.R. Horton's lot purchases. Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C10; calculation C11; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

spans.text: ## Request

Forestar Group Inc. (issuer id for-1406587), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the financial foundation: statements, debt, liquidity and calculated credit measures for the fiscal years ended September 30, 2022 to 2025 and the interim periods to June 30, 2026, from four SEC filings.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-09-30_for-20240930.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2024 | 2024-11-19 | bee6a60c48b3935475a888b00b54cadb54ec9d4a7d9c257e02e3272824e5aa61 | FY2022 and FY2023 income statements and cash flows, the 2023-09-30 balance sheet, 2023 debt and interest figures, and 2024 facility terms |

| 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025 | 2025-11-19 | 90b514e588fb4fbba0b3573de81bea98eb99807f39d2abdb328f14d1e9cd88af | Latest audited statements for FY2023 to FY2025, the debt note, facility terms, capitalized interest note, debt retirements and surety bonds |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_for-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2026 | 2026-04-23 | 0ab1a8d88fc4c759b0d688746280b126a1af01cd54f14fa683bc0d20ab11dd1c | Six-month statements and the 2026-03-31 balance sheet, debt, facility availability and interest incurred |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2026 | 2026-07-22 | 3bf6e7e5bde1d95509c4adba55c0105be63473daa381d28e516481ef4815a12b | Nine-month and third-quarter statements, the 2026-06-30 balance sheet, debt, facility, liquidity, commitments, fair value and related-party items |
| Module | Handoff | sha256 | Use |

| CP-0 | Source readiness | e2f2fb4196cc15f2815e8ef1b06d7329366496aa18ce798bce561f7b4f16b34f | Source set, limitations, cutoff gap and the facility, covenant and rating gaps carried into this module |
No web or external source was used, and the run settings are not evidence. The two annual reports are audited; the two quarterly reports are unaudited.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Forestar's debt is moderate and its liquidity is large relative to it, so creditors face little refinancing pressure before March 2028, but interest cover cannot be shown on cash because the filings print no cash interest paid. Total debt of USD 793.8 million was 3.13x last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 253.7 million at June 30, 2026 and net debt of USD 398.9 million was 1.57x, on an EBITDA this analysis calculates because the issuer prints none.
Basis: calculation K03; calculation K05; calculation K06; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4

The pressure point is cash generation: operating cash flow was negative in fiscal 2024 and 2025 while inventory grew, and turned positive at USD 27.6 million only in the nine months to June 30, 2026. Cash and undrawn revolver capacity of USD 1,064.8 million cover debt 1.34x, but USD 65.0 million of that capacity was scheduled to mature on October 28, 2026 with no outcome established.
Basis: calculation K10; calculation K12; calculation K11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 24
### Key findings

Net leverage rose from 0.33x at the 2023 year end to 1.71x at the 2025 year end because the company turned cash into inventory, not because earnings fell: real estate grew from USD 1,790.3 million to USD 2,645.1 million while cash fell from USD 616.0 million to USD 379.2 million, fiscal 2025 added a net USD 100.0 million of debt, and EBITDA was USD 237.8 million in fiscal 2023 and USD 247.2 million in fiscal 2025. By June 30, 2026 net leverage had eased to 1.57x as inventory growth slowed: cash put into real estate was USD 69.3 million in the nine months against USD 561.0 million a year earlier. Leverage here is therefore set by how fast the company invests in land, which management controls, and it will rise again if the fiscal 2025 pace of investment returns without matching earnings growth.

Basis: calculation K04; calculation K06; calculation K18; calculation K23; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-K_2024-09-30_for-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4

EBITDA was USD 237.8 million in fiscal 2023, USD 281.4 million in fiscal 2024 and USD 247.2 million in fiscal 2025. The fiscal 2025 fall came from selling, general and administrative expense rising from USD 118.5 million to USD 154.4 million and from gross margin slipping from 23.80% to 21.87%, only partly offset by revenue growth to USD 1,662.4 million. In the nine months to June 30, 2026 revenue rose 6.29% on tract and other land sales of USD 90.4 million against USD 14.6 million, while residential lot sales revenue slipped from USD 977.3 million to USD 963.9 million and gross margin eased to 20.80%; EBITDA grew only from USD 121.2 million to USD 127.7 million. The earnings base that supports the debt has not recovered to the fiscal 2024 level, and the land sales that drive growth are lumpy.
Basis: calculation K01; calculation K13; calculation K14; calculation K25; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2

Cash interest cover cannot be calculated: the cash flow statements print no interest paid, and all interest incurred is capitalized to real estate and released to cost of sales as lots are sold. Interest incurred rose from USD 32.6 million in fiscal 2024 to USD 45.5 million in fiscal 2025 after the 6.5% 2033 notes replaced the 3.85% 2026 notes. On that accrual proxy EBITDA cover fell from 8.63x to 5.43x and is 5.01x for the twelve months to June 30, 2026; the two notes alone carry USD 47.5 million of annual coupons, which twelve-month EBITDA covers 5.34x. The cash figure may differ because coupons are paid semiannually: accrued interest was USD 14.4 million at June 30, 2026 against USD 2.5 million at September 30, 2025. Cover stays at or above 5.01x on these proxies, but the direction since fiscal 2024 is down and no cash evidence confirms the level.

Basis: calculation K07; calculation K08; calculation K24; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 67; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9

Operating cash flow was USD 364.1 million in fiscal 2023, when real estate fell by USD 206.3 million, then an outflow of USD 158.4 million in fiscal 2024 and USD 197.7 million in fiscal 2025 as real estate grew. EBITDA therefore overstates cash available for debt service in investment years and understates it in harvest years: free cash flow before debt service was USD 362.8 million in fiscal 2023 and an outflow of USD 199.9 million in fiscal 2025. Seasonality matters for the current year: the nine months to June 30, 2026 show free cash flow of USD 27.3 million, but the twelve months to that date show USD 282.9 million because the fiscal fourth quarter is the strongest delivery quarter.

Basis: calculation K15; calculation K03; calculation K23; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 27

At June 30, 2026 the company held USD 394.9 million of cash and USD 669.9 million of undrawn revolver capacity after USD 45.1 million of letters of credit, a total of USD 1,064.8 million or 1.34x total debt. All debt is senior unsecured and ranks equally: USD 300.0 million of 5.0% notes due 2028, USD 500.0 million of 6.5% notes due 2033 and an undrawn revolver, with no principal due for 20 months after the balance-sheet date. Availability is limited by a borrowing base tied to the book value of real estate and unrestricted cash, which the filings do not quantify, and USD 65.0 million of the commitments was scheduled to mature on October 28, 2026; without it availability would be USD 604.9 million and liquidity USD 999.8 million.

Basis: calculation K09; calculation K10; calculation K11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24

Several claims sit outside the debt figure. Earnest money deposits of USD 202.2 million, 25.47% of total debt and up from USD 121.4 million at the 2023 year end, are customer funds that finance inventory and are released as lots are sold, and they are subject to mortgages secured by the real estate under contract; the filings do not name the lienholder, but such liens would sit ahead of the unsecured notes and revolver on those lots to the extent of the deposits. Surety bonds of USD 874.3 million and letters of credit of USD 45.1 million support development obligations, lease liabilities are USD 16.4 million, and a pledged reimbursements liability of USD 22.4 million is matched by an asset of the same size with no recourse to the company. Land purchase contracts carry a remaining price of USD 615.9 million against deposits of USD 33.7 million and are options, not obligations.

Basis: calculation K17; calculation K24; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15

The one price indication in the filings shows no stress: the fair value of debt was USD 807.8 million against principal of USD 800.0 million, 100.98% of principal, on quotes from inactive markets. This is not a market-implied risk assessment, but it gives no sign that lenders discount the notes.
Basis: calculation K19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 16

EBITDA is the main definition risk because the issuer prints none. This analysis adds interest charged to cost of sales and depreciation to income before income taxes and removes interest and other income. Without the interest add-back, twelve-month EBITDA would be USD 221.3 million and total debt 3.59x, so the add-back moves leverage by 0.46x; a reader who treats capitalized interest as an operating cost should use the lower EBITDA.
Basis: calculation K01; calculation K20; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 67; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 7

No event after June 30, 2026 that changes net debt is stated in the filings, which end with the quarterly report signed on July 22, 2026; the only dated forward item is the USD 65.0 million revolver tranche due October 28, 2026, which does not change net debt because the revolver is undrawn. Earlier events were kept out of period figures: the October 30, 2025 increase of USD 25.0 million in revolver commitments, the December 2025 repayment of the USD 9.9 million other note payable, which lowered debt and cash together and left net debt unchanged, and the March 2026 increase of USD 50.0 million in commitments.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation K10; calculation K26

The retirement of the 2026 notes shows one event in several figures: principal retired was USD 400.0 million (USD 329.4 million tendered and USD 70.6 million redeemed), cash paid was USD 405.0 million including USD 5.2 million of accrued interest, the loss recorded was USD 1.2 million, and the repayment of debt line of USD 680.0 million in the cash flow statement also holds USD 280.0 million of revolver repayments. The principal serves the debt history, the cash flow line serves cash movements and the loss serves earnings.
Basis: calculation K18; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 70
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against caution is the issuer's own measure: net debt to total capital was 17.7% at June 30, 2026 against a stated long-term aim of approximately 40% or less, no covenant breach is reported, and contracted lot sales to the controlling shareholder have a remaining sales price of USD 2,095.1 million against earnest money of USD 195.3 million. The cautious reading would fall away if covenant levels and the borrowing base proved wide, if cash interest paid matched the accrual proxy, and if operating cash flow stayed positive through the fiscal fourth quarter. It would harden if the annual report for fiscal 2026 showed operating outflows of the fiscal 2025 size with EBITDA below USD 247.2 million, or if the October 28, 2026 revolver tranche lapsed without replacement.
Basis: calculation K16; calculation K24; calculation K11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 23
### Limitations

EBITDA is an analyst calculation and its interim inputs are unaudited. Cash interest paid, covenant levels, borrowing-base amounts and credit ratings are not printed. The first quarter of fiscal 2026 has no report of its own, so only cumulative interim periods are tabulated. Nothing after July 22, 2026 is supplied, so the October 28, 2026 revolver outcome, fiscal 2026 results and any later financing are not established. Dash cells in the statements are treated as missing, not zero, and the guarantor list is not printed.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 31

spans.text: ## Request

Forestar Group Inc. (issuer id for-1406587), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope is business, ownership, governance and sponsor-behaviour facts, the 2025 refinancing and the issuer's dated history, from four SEC filings and the source readiness assessment.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-09-30_for-20240930.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2024 | 2024-11-19 | bee6a60c48b3935475a888b00b54cadb54ec9d4a7d9c257e02e3272824e5aa61 | History, lot sales to D.R. Horton and other customers for FY2023 and FY2024, equity issued in fiscal 2024, and the earlier lot position |

| 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025 | 2025-11-19 | 90b514e588fb4fbba0b3573de81bea98eb99807f39d2abdb328f14d1e9cd88af | Business, control rights, risk factors, related-party note, litigation, exhibits and the signature page |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_for-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2026 | 2026-04-23 | 0ab1a8d88fc4c759b0d688746280b126a1af01cd54f14fa683bc0d20ab11dd1c | Facility commitments in March 2026 and the ownership level at that date |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2026 | 2026-07-22 | 3bf6e7e5bde1d95509c4adba55c0105be63473daa381d28e516481ef4815a12b | Latest ownership, related-party flows, litigation, lot position, operating results and facility terms |
| Module | Handoff | sha256 | Use |
| CP-0 | Source readiness | e2f2fb4196cc15f2815e8ef1b06d7329366496aa18ce798bce561f7b4f16b34f | Source set, cutoff gap and the missing proxy statement and executed agreements |
No web or external source was used, and the run settings are not evidence.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Forestar is a parent-controlled lot developer: D.R. Horton owns about 62%, bought 82.79% of lot sales revenues in fiscal 2025 and can veto debt above 40% leverage, so creditors get steady contracted demand but carry conflict risk and no stated parent support.
Basis: calculation B01; calculation B10; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 41

No dividend, buyback or other extraction is documented, the 2025 refinancing moved the first note maturity to 2028, and the parent's lot contracts carry USD 2,095.1 million of remaining sales price, but a stockholder suit alleges breach of fiduciary duty in lot sales to the parent and the executed agreements are not supplied. Governance risk is medium.
Basis: calculation B04; calculation B11; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15
### Key findings

Control sits with one industrial parent, and no parent guarantee or support for the Company's debt is stated. D.R. Horton owns about 62% of the common stock, designates four of seven directors and the Executive Chairman, and while it holds at least 35% must consent to new equity classes, executive changes, certain acquisitions and debt that takes total leverage above 40%. The consent right limits releveraging by the Company alone, but it also gives the parent a veto over refinancing choices; the filings do not define total leverage for this test, so it is not established as a creditor protection.
Basis: calculation B10; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4

Revenue is concentrated in the controlling shareholder, so the Company's cash flow is a function of one buyer's demand. D.R. Horton accounted for 82.79% of residential lot sales revenues in fiscal 2025 and 85.97% in the nine months to June 30, 2026, against 82.89% a year earlier, and 80.61% of total revenues once tract sales are counted. Lot bankers that expect to resell to D.R. Horton add indirect dependence: USD 83.4 million of lots in fiscal 2025 and USD 33.4 million in the nine months. Contract strength partly offsets this, with USD 2,095.1 million of remaining sales price on owned lots under contract to the parent and USD 195.3 million of earnest money, 9.32% of that price.

Basis: calculation B01; calculation B02; calculation B04; calculation B12; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21

The supply relationship is long but not binding on the parent. The Master Supply Agreement runs until June 29, 2037 or until D.R. Horton falls below 15% of voting shares, and the parent holds a right of first offer on lots, not an obligation to buy; it is not required to present land opportunities and is not restricted from competing, and lot sales contracts require an earnest money deposit that the Company may retain or refund on cancellation depending on the contract. The deposit is a modest share of the remaining price, so contracted revenue rests on the parent's willingness to close as much as on the deposit.
Basis: calculation B04; calculation B10; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–16; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15

Related-party costs are modest, but the pricing of lots to the parent is contested. Shared-service, benefit and other costs paid to the parent were USD 23.3 million in fiscal 2025, 15.09% of selling, general and administrative expense, and the Company reimbursed the parent USD 47.1 million for earnest money and diligence costs on contracts it then closed itself; neither looks like extraction on this evidence. A derivative complaint filed on April 29, 2025 alleges breach of fiduciary duty in lot sales between the Company and the parent, no loss is estimated and the Company disputes it, so a settlement or ruling that changed lot terms could affect the Company's revenue; no such change is stated.
Basis: calculation B06; calculation B07; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 78–79; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 13

Financial policy has been creditor-aligned on distributions and maturities. The Company pays no dividend and intends to retain earnings, raised USD 19.7 million of equity in fiscal 2024 and none since while holding USD 300.0 million of program capacity, and in 2025 issued USD 500.0 million of 6.5% notes due 2033 to retire the 2026 notes, so no note matures before March 2028. The cost is a higher coupon, and legal capacity for dividends, related-party payments and added debt cannot be assessed because the indentures and credit agreement are not supplied.

Basis: calculation B11; calculation B12; 10-K_2024-09-30_for-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12

The business model limits some risks and concentrates others. The Company develops entitled, short-duration projects in phases across 65 markets in 24 states, so no single market dominates, but substantially all development work is subcontracted and lot demand is under affordability pressure: in the nine months to June 30, 2026 lots sold fell 8.64% while the average price rose 8.13%, so residential lot sales revenues fell 1.37%. Real estate rose USD 378.9 million in fiscal 2025, which commits cash to land ahead of sales.

Basis: calculation B08; calculation B09; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 18–20

Disclosure supports monitoring of reported figures but not of control terms. The statements are audited with an unqualified opinion and effective internal control, lenders receive quarterly covenant reports, and the Company has not used its controlled-company exemptions, but director independence, pay, beneficial ownership and the executed agreements sit in documents that are not supplied.

Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 81–82; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a lower risk view is behavioural and contractual: the Company has paid no dividend, the parent's leverage consent right works as a cap on debt, and its lot contracts carry USD 2,095.1 million of remaining sales price backed by USD 195.3 million of earnest money under a supply agreement that runs to 2037. The view would improve if the executed agreements showed firm purchase obligations and a defined leverage test, if the derivative suit were dismissed, and if the parent's own credit quality were shown to be strong. It would worsen if D.R. Horton fell below 35%, which ends its consent rights, or below 20%, which ends its board designation rights, if lot prices to the parent were reset, if its lot purchases fell, or if the Company paid a dividend or a related-party payment out of debt-funded cash.
Basis: calculation B04; calculation B10; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15
### Limitations

- The executed Stockholder's, Master Supply and Shared Services agreements are not supplied, so the consent rights, the 40% leverage test and the lot pricing rules rest on summaries; this keeps the view that the consent right protects creditors unestablished.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 84

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so the conclusion on board balance rests on the annual report's statement that D.R. Horton may designate four of seven directors; how many directors are independent is not established.
- D.R. Horton's own financial condition and credit rating are not in the sources, so the strength of the main customer, on which the concentration finding depends, is not assessed.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- No indenture or credit agreement is supplied, so legal capacity for dividends, related-party payments and added debt is not established; the finding of no extraction rests on behaviour alone and would change if large unused capacity were shown.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 83–85
- The sources stop at the quarterly report signed on July 22, 2026, so any change in D.R. Horton's holding, in the derivative suit or in the contract position after June 30, 2026 is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 31

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

D.R. Horton became the controlling shareholder in October 2017 under a merger agreement dated June 29, 2017 and owned 75% of the common stock afterwards; it owned about 62% at September 30, 2025 and at June 30, 2026, and the filings do not describe how the holding fell.

New debt in the period is a refinancing, not growth capital. In March 2025 the Company issued USD 500.0 million of 6.5% senior notes due 2033 and tendered for its 2026 notes, of which USD 329.4 million was tendered, and in September 2025 it redeemed the remaining USD 70.6 million, so no note matures before March 2028. The revolver grew from USD 410.0 million of commitments at September 30, 2024 to USD 640.0 million a year later, then to USD 665.0 million after October 30, 2025 and USD 715.0 million after March 2026, with USD 650.0 million maturing in December 2029 and USD 65.0 million in October 2026; a USD 9.9 million secured note was repaid in December 2025.

Equity access is unused: an at-the-market program raised USD 19.7 million in fiscal 2024, and a new program of USD 300.0 million under a USD 750.0 million shelf has issued nothing. No business acquisition, disposal, dividend or recapitalisation is reported in the period.

spans.text: ## Request

Forestar Group Inc. (issuer id for-1406587), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the fundamental credit synthesis: business model, ownership, earnings and cash-flow durability, liquidity, refinancing, downside and monitoring, built on four SEC filings and the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance modules.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-09-30_for-20240930.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2024 | 2024-11-19 | bee6a60c48b3935475a888b00b54cadb54ec9d4a7d9c257e02e3272824e5aa61 | Earlier years for earnings, cash flow and real estate, and lot sales by buyer for FY2023 and FY2024 |

| 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025 | 2025-11-19 | 90b514e588fb4fbba0b3573de81bea98eb99807f39d2abdb328f14d1e9cd88af | Business, competition, seasonality, risk factors, audited FY2025 statements, debt and the 2025 refinancing |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_for-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2026 | 2026-04-23 | 0ab1a8d88fc4c759b0d688746280b126a1af01cd54f14fa683bc0d20ab11dd1c | Facility commitments and interest at the half year, read for continuity only |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2026 | 2026-07-22 | 3bf6e7e5bde1d95509c4adba55c0105be63473daa381d28e516481ef4815a12b | Latest balance sheet, cash flows, debt, liquidity, lot position, contracts with D.R. Horton, market commentary and facility terms |
| Module | Handoff | sha256 | Use |

| CP-1 | Financial foundation | c1e0aace509c5e23f4d80b394d3146aee829a0f4b77083626c0c7fff4cd2bdee | Statements, calculated EBITDA, debt, liquidity and leverage figures restated in the calculations |

| CP-1A | Business & governance | d3c43201d1d6befef19f42cfeba285f0ab67971c2226c56fcb1ba2f2444a6e9c | Ownership, consent rights, concentration, related-party flows, the derivative suit and financial policy behaviour |
No web or external source was used, and the run settings are not evidence.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Forestar is an adequate credit: modest leverage and large liquidity cover its debt, but its controlling shareholder, D.R. Horton, buys most of its lots, so creditors depend on that parent's continued purchases. Total debt of USD 793.8 million is 3.13x last-twelve-months (LTM) EBITDA (calculated here because the issuer prints none) and net debt is 1.57x, while liquidity of USD 1,064.8 million is 3.55x the USD 300.0 million of notes due March 2028, with no principal due for 20 months.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 24; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The weak point is cash flow: free cash flow was USD 2.3 million over fiscal 2023 to 2025 against USD 766.4 million of EBITDA, because earnings were reinvested in land, so leverage depends on spending that management controls. The main downside path is a slower parent taking fewer lots at lower prices while development spending continues.
Basis: calculation C03; calculation C11; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 60; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Key findings

Dependence on one controlling customer is the dominant credit risk, because that customer sets both the volume and the price of most revenue. D.R. Horton owns about 62% of the common stock, bought 82.79% of residential lot sales revenues in fiscal 2025 and 85.97% in the nine months to June 30, 2026 (82.89% a year earlier), and has USD 2,095.1 million of remaining sales price under contract with earnest money of only 9.32% of it. The supply agreement gives the parent a right of first offer, not a purchase obligation, no parent guarantee of the debt is stated, and a derivative suit alleges breach of fiduciary duty in lot sale transactions with the parent, so creditors rely on the parent's choice to keep buying at acceptable prices.

Basis: calculation C10; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 20

Whether the parent buys lots below market prices cannot be shown, and the evidence is mixed and distorted by regional mix. Derived average revenue per lot to D.R. Horton was USD 111,347 in the nine months to June 30, 2026, 9.97% below USD 123,675 for other customers, and 11.57% and 6.71% below in fiscal 2023 and fiscal 2024, but 1.89% above in fiscal 2025 (6.79% below once the USD 83.4 million of lots sold to a lot banker that expects to resell to the parent are excluded) and 4.69% above in the nine months to June 30, 2025. The filings attribute price changes mainly to regional mix and print no margin by customer, so the data neither confirm nor rule out below-market pricing; a ruling or settlement in the derivative suit that changed lot terms could move revenue either way and could change the parent's buying, so creditors should treat pricing as an uncertainty, not a source of upside.

Basis: calculation C16; calculation C10; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2024-09-30_for-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 20

Liquidity is the main support and covers the first maturity several times. Cash of USD 394.9 million and undrawn revolver capacity of USD 669.9 million after USD 45.1 million of letters of credit total USD 1,064.8 million, 1.34x total debt and 3.55x the USD 300.0 million of 5.0% notes due March 1, 2028, which is 20 months after the balance-sheet date. If the USD 65.0 million revolver tranche that was scheduled to mature on October 28, 2026 lapsed without replacement, liquidity would be USD 999.8 million, still 3.33x those notes; availability is limited by a borrowing base tied to the book value of real estate and unrestricted cash, which the filings do not quantify.

Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 24

Cash generation is the weakest link, because inventory absorbs the earnings. Free cash flow was USD 2.3 million over fiscal 2023 to 2025 against USD 766.4 million of EBITDA, with outflows of USD 160.6 million in fiscal 2024 and USD 199.9 million in fiscal 2025 while, over those two years, real estate grew USD 854.8 million and net debt rose USD 344.5 million. The nine months to June 30, 2026 turned positive, with free cash flow of USD 27.3 million, because net cash put into real estate fell USD 491.7 million, to USD 69.3 million, and the fiscal fourth quarter of 2025 alone produced USD 256.3 million of operating cash flow. Spending can therefore be slowed quickly, but the cash result follows the pace of land investment and the seasonal timing of lot deliveries, not a stable conversion of earnings.

Basis: calculation C03; calculation C04; 10-K_2024-09-30_for-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Low leverage is a policy choice, not a constraint, so it should not be read as a lasting protection. Net debt to total capital was 17.7% at June 30, 2026 against 28.9% a year earlier, a fall of 11.2 percentage points, but the issuer's long-term aim is approximately 40% or less, which would allow net debt of USD 1,237.7 million, USD 838.8 million more than today and 4.88x LTM EBITDA with equity held constant. The only printed external brake is the parent's consent to debt that takes total leverage above 40%, a term the filings do not define, so the cushion that exists today depends on management and the controlling shareholder choosing not to use it.
Basis: calculation C08; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 23

Earnings have not recovered to the fiscal 2024 level and operating leverage turned against the company in fiscal 2025. EBITDA fell from USD 281.4 million to USD 247.2 million because selling, general and administrative expense, called overhead below, rose 30.30% while gross profit rose only USD 4.2 million, and gross margin eased 0.76 percentage points to 20.80% in the nine months to June 30, 2026. The USD 62.4 million of revenue growth in those nine months came from tract and other land sales, up USD 75.8 million, while residential lot sales revenues fell USD 13.4 million, so the recurring line is shrinking and the growth line is lumpy; overhead was stable at USD 112.6 million against USD 111.8 million, which limits the pressure, and management says lot prices were reduced where necessary.

Basis: calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C07; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19

Refinancing risk is low until 2028 and then rests on market access for the USD 300.0 million of 5.0% notes. Refinancing them at the 6.5% coupon of the 2033 notes would add USD 4.5 million of annual interest and lower EBITDA cover of coupons from 5.34x to 4.88x; all USD 800.0 million of principal is senior unsecured and ranks equally, the weighted coupon is 5.94% and the only price indication, a fair value of 100.98% of principal, shows no discount. EBITDA covers interest incurred 5.01x, but all interest is capitalized, so cash cover cannot be shown, and the revolver's USD 650.0 million commitments mature on December 18, 2029.

Basis: calculation C12; calculation C13; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 16; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Book-value cover is wide but is not a recovery estimate. Debt is 58.25% of total liabilities, real estate of USD 2,711.5 million is 3.42x debt and total assets are 2.36x total liabilities, yet only 15.43% of owned lots are fully developed, so most of the carrying value is land and work in progress whose realizable value depends on the housing market. Other liabilities of USD 569.0 million include USD 202.2 million of customer earnest money that finances inventory and is subject to mortgages secured by the real estate under contract; those mortgages would rank ahead of unsecured creditors on the lots concerned, and the filings do not name their holder. Surety bonds of USD 874.3 million and letters of credit of USD 45.1 million support development obligations off the balance sheet, and lease liabilities of USD 16.4 million sit inside accrued expenses, so none of these is in the debt figure.

Basis: calculation C04; calculation C09; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 23; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a better view is that the balance sheet improved in the same season: net debt to total capital was 17.7% at June 30, 2026 against 28.9% a year earlier, operating cash flow turned positive with no borrowing on the revolver, no dividend has been paid and the parent holds USD 2,095.1 million of contracted remaining sales price. If fiscal 2026 shows positive operating cash flow for the full year, EBITDA at or above USD 253.7 million and a replacement for the revolver tranche, the view would move toward strong on liquidity and leverage. The strongest evidence for a worse view is concentration: the parent's share of lot revenues rose from 82.89% to 85.97% between the two nine-month periods while lots sold fell 8.64%, and no purchase obligation exists. The view would weaken if that share passed the fiscal 2024 level of 87.30% while volumes fell, if net cash put into real estate returned to the nine-month 2025 pace of USD 561.0 million with EBITDA below USD 247.2 million, which would put net debt above 1.71x EBITDA, or if the parent's holding fell below 35%.

Basis: calculation C08; calculation C10; calculation C04; calculation C01; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 23
### Limitations

- The fiscal fourth quarter of 2026 ended on September 30, 2026, before the as-of date, but no result for it is supplied; because that quarter is seasonally the strongest for cash, the view that cash generation has turned positive rests on nine months and could reverse or strengthen once the full year is known.

- The sources contain no peer or sector benchmark, so the comparison of Forestar with typical leveraged issuers is analyst judgement, and the adequate assessment of the business profile is relative to the issuer's own record, not to other lot developers.

- No margin by customer is printed, and the average revenue per lot derived by customer is distorted by regional mix and lot-banker sales, so whether the parent pays above or below market, and how group margin would hold if it bought fewer lots, is not established.
Basis: calculation C16; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 20

- The downside leverage figures rest on analyst-chosen sensitivities, a 12.44% and a 25% fall in EBITDA and a repeat of the fiscal 2025 cash outflow, and the sources do not split overhead between fixed and variable cost; they show direction and scale, not probability.
Basis: calculation C11; calculation C06
### Strengths and weaknesses

The first strength is the liquidity runway: cash of USD 394.9 million and undrawn revolver capacity of USD 669.9 million total USD 1,064.8 million, 3.55x the USD 300.0 million of notes due March 2028, so a closed debt market would not force a payment default before then and near-term default and refinancing risk are low.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 24

The second strength is modest leverage: total debt is 3.13x and net debt 1.57x LTM EBITDA and net debt to total capital is 17.7%, so even a repeat of the largest annual EBITDA decline in the sources, 12.44%, would leave net debt at 1.80x EBITDA and the debt serviceable from earnings.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 23

The third strength is revenue visibility from contracted lots: USD 2,095.1 million of remaining sales price is under contract with D.R. Horton with earnest money of 9.32% of it, so deliveries in the generally three to eighteen months between signing and closing are largely known, although the filings show no firm obligation beyond the deposit and cancellation terms vary by contract.
Basis: calculation C10; calculation C15; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15

The fourth strength is flexible land spending: net cash put into real estate fell USD 491.7 million year on year, and land purchase contracts with a remaining price of USD 615.9 million carry deposits of only USD 33.7 million, so commitments can be cut faster than revenue falls, which protects liquidity in a downturn, although the company expects to buy most of the land within 3 years and no contract carries specific performance.
Basis: calculation C04; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 14

The fifth strength is the debt structure: all USD 800.0 million of principal is senior unsecured with no maturity until March 2028, and the 2025 issue of USD 500.0 million of 2033 notes already moved the first maturity out, so the next refinancing is about 15 months from the as-of date and is covered 3.55x by liquidity.
Basis: calculation C02; calculation C12; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9

The first weakness is concentration in the controlling customer: D.R. Horton bought 82.79% of residential lot sales revenues in fiscal 2025 and 85.97% in the nine months to June 30, 2026, so one buyer's demand and pricing decide revenue and cash flow, and a slowdown in its purchases would hit creditors first through lower lot sales while development spending continues.
Basis: calculation C10; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 20

The second weakness is cash flow that follows inventory spending: free cash flow was USD 2.3 million over fiscal 2023 to 2025 against USD 766.4 million of EBITDA, so earnings do not accumulate as cash in growth years and leverage rises with land investment.
Basis: calculation C03; calculation C04; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 60

The third weakness is earnings erosion and operating leverage: EBITDA fell 12.15% in fiscal 2025 because overhead rose 30.30% against gross profit growth of USD 4.2 million, and gross margin eased 0.76 percentage points in the latest nine months, which weakens coverage if margins keep slipping.
Basis: calculation C06; calculation C07; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2

The fourth weakness is low-quality revenue growth: lots sold fell 8.64% while the average price rose 8.13%, residential lot sales revenues fell USD 13.4 million and all of the USD 62.4 million of revenue growth came from lumpy tract and other land sales, so growth may not recur.
Basis: calculation C05; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 20

The fifth weakness is a financial policy that permits much more debt: the issuer's aim of approximately 40% net debt to total capital would allow net debt of USD 1,237.7 million, 3.10x today's level, so low leverage today is not a lasting protection.
Basis: calculation C08; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 23

### Business model, ownership and financial policy

Forestar acquires and entitles land, develops it into finished residential lots and sells them mainly to homebuilders in 65 markets across 24 states, with a lot position of 91,700 lots, of which 62,200 are owned and 29,500 are controlled through purchase contracts. Projects are entitled, short-duration and phased, substantially all development work is subcontracted and fixed assets are negligible, so capital is tied up for a limited period per phase; the cost is that real estate of USD 2,711.5 million is 84.19% of total assets, financed by equity, debt and USD 202.2 million of customer deposits. Cash-flow visibility therefore comes from contracts and delivery timing, not from recurring revenue, and debt service capacity depends on lots closing.
Basis: calculation C09; calculation C14; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 23

D.R. Horton controls the company with about 62% of the common stock, designates four of seven directors, and must consent while it holds at least 35% to debt that takes total leverage above 40%; the Master Supply Agreement runs to June 29, 2037 and gives it a right of first offer on lots, and the company relies on it for shared services. No dividend, repurchase or parent funding is documented, equity of USD 19.7 million was raised in fiscal 2024 and none since, and the issuer aims to keep net debt to total capital at approximately 40% or less. The revolver carries financial covenants for minimum tangible net worth, minimum liquidity and maximum leverage whose levels are not printed, and the filings say the parent's interests may differ from those of other holders, so creditor alignment is partial: the parent is a supportive customer and a controlling shareholder at the same time.

Basis: calculation C08; calculation C10; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8
### Revenue, margin and cash-flow durability

Revenue is transactional, cyclical, concentrated and partly contracted rather than recurring. Lot sales close three to eighteen months after contract, 37.78% of owned lots are under contract and the fiscal fourth quarter is seasonally the strongest, so no single quarter represents the year. Price and volume moved in opposite directions in the nine months to June 30, 2026, with lots sold down 8.64% and the average price up 8.13%, at a time when management says builders are using incentives to address affordability; revenue visibility is therefore up to eighteen months, and the pricing power shown depends on the parent accepting higher prices.

Basis: calculation C05; calculation C10; calculation C15; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 20

Margin resilience is average. Gross margin was 21.16% in fiscal 2023, 23.80% in fiscal 2024, 21.87% in fiscal 2025 and 20.80% in the nine months to June 30, 2026, management raises prices only when market conditions permit and has reduced them where necessary, and overhead rose 30.30% in fiscal 2025 before stabilizing at USD 112.6 million in the latest nine months. The sources do not split overhead between fixed and variable cost, so margin defence under volume pressure cannot be modelled; development costs remain elevated and municipal delays extend cycle times.
Basis: calculation C06; calculation C07; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19

Capital intensity is in inventory, not fixed assets: capex was only 0.89% of fiscal 2025 EBITDA, so free cash flow is operating cash flow and the swing factor is real estate spending. Gross investment in acquisition and development was USD 1,006.0 million in the nine months to June 30, 2026, yet net cash put into real estate was only USD 69.3 million because lots sold released carrying value, and conversion of EBITDA to free cash flow was 0.30% over three fiscal years against a ratio of 1.12x in the twelve months to June 30, 2026, which includes the strong fourth quarter of fiscal 2025. Capex flexibility over the 2028 and 2033 maturities is high, but earnings translate into cash for debt service only in years when land spending is held back.
Basis: calculation C03; calculation C04; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 6
### Competitive forces

Competitive rivalry is high and the market is fragmented: the annual report names numerous local, regional and national developers and homebuilders, some larger or with a lower cost of capital, and says competition can make it hard to buy or sell land at acceptable returns. The credit translation is limited pricing power outside the parent relationship, but also no single rival that threatens volume.

The threat of new entrants is moderate in the analyst's judgement: entitlement skill and capital protect the business, but national homebuilders can develop their own lots and the parent is not restricted from competing, so the barrier does not secure the parent's purchases for creditors.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 14

The threat of substitutes is the parent sourcing lots elsewhere or developing them itself, which the filings do not prevent: it is not required to present land opportunities to the company and is not restricted from competing, its right of first offer is not an obligation, and lot bankers that expect to resell to it bought USD 83.4 million of lots in fiscal 2025 as an indirect channel, which caps the revenue support from contracted lots.
Basis: calculation C10; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 41

Buyer power is very high, since one buyer accounts for 82.79% of lot sales revenues; it determines timing and price and is also the controlling shareholder, which is the largest force on default probability and recovery.
Basis: calculation C10; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 41

Supplier power is moderate: land sellers gain bargaining power when competition is high, subcontractors are chosen by competitive bid, and steel, transformers and concrete are exposed to commodity prices and, for steel, tariffs, so cost inflation can compress margin when selling prices cannot rise.
### External factors

Political and regulatory factors are a secondary driver: tariffs on imported steel, aluminum and lumber can raise home costs and so pressure builders' affordability, municipal approval delays extend development cycles and tie up capital longer, and reimbursement of infrastructure costs depends on district bond issuance, so a weak bond market could delay cash recovery on some projects.

Economic factors are the main external driver: mortgage rates have stayed elevated since 2022, builders use incentives, and the resulting affordability constraint sets lot demand and price, which feeds directly into revenue, margin and operating cash flow. Social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials.
### SWOT in credit terms

Strengths in credit terms are the liquidity runway, modest leverage, contracted lots, flexible land spending and unsecured term debt; they are ranked with their mechanisms in the strengths and weaknesses selector above.

Weaknesses in credit terms are the customer and control concentration, cash flow that follows inventory spending, earnings erosion, shrinking recurring lot revenue and a policy that permits much more debt.

Opportunities that could improve credit quality are slower land spending with stable earnings, which would cut net leverage further, lower policy interest rates, which the annual report says have been reduced since the increases of 2022 and 2023 and may fall further and would help affordability if mortgage rates follow, and tract and other land sales, which rose to USD 90.4 million in the nine months to June 30, 2026 from USD 14.6 million, mostly to customers other than the parent, and would reduce reliance on it if they recur.
Basis: calculation C05; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21

Threats that could weaken credit quality are prolonged elevated mortgage rates, tariffs and approval delays that raise costs, the derivative suit over lot sale transactions with the parent, a fall in the parent's holding below the 35% consent threshold, and an unreplaced revolver tranche.

Basis: calculation C10; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8
### Financial profile and credit quality

The financial profile is adequate. Liquidity is the strongest dimension and access to capital markets is average, shown by the 2025 refinancing and a fair value of debt at 100.98% of principal; scale, competitive advantage, margin stability, cost flexibility and financial policy are average, and free cash flow stability and customer diversification are the weakest dimensions. The main supports are liquidity of USD 1,064.8 million and net debt of 1.57x EBITDA; the main constraints are the single customer and cash flow that follows inventory. The trend is mixed: net debt to EBITDA rose from 0.33x in fiscal 2023 to 1.71x in fiscal 2025 and eased to 1.57x in the twelve months to June 30, 2026, while EBITDA moved from USD 237.8 million to USD 281.4 million, USD 247.2 million and USD 253.7 million. The datapoints that would settle the view are cash interest paid, covenant levels and compliance headroom, the borrowing base, price by customer and D.R. Horton's own credit quality.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C12; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Outlook

Over the next 12 to 24 months management describes demand as held back by affordability and cautious consumer sentiment with elevated builder incentives, yet third-quarter revenues rose 4.23% and net cash put into real estate has been cut; the sector headwind is elevated mortgage rates and the company headwind is lower lot volume at higher prices. The notes due March 1, 2028 fall inside this window, about 15 months after the as-of date, and the 2028 notes became redeemable at par after March 1, 2026, so refinancing can begin early; the outcome of the revolver tranche scheduled for October 28, 2026 and the results for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026 are not established. The implication for revenue and margin is pressure; for liquidity and refinancing it is stability, with deleveraging dependent on land spending staying low.

Basis: calculation C02; calculation C05; calculation C12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 24

Over three to five years the USD 650.0 million of revolver commitments matures on December 18, 2029, about three years after the as-of date, the 2033 notes mature on March 15, 2033 and the supply agreement with D.R. Horton runs to June 29, 2037, so the credit depends on the housing cycle, the parent's share of purchases and whether management moves net debt toward its 40% aim. Sector tailwinds are policy rates that the annual report says have been lowered and may fall further, and a focus on entry-level homes, the segment where housing demand has been highest; company tailwinds are liquidity and low leverage; company headwinds are concentration, margins and cash flow tied to inventory.
Basis: calculation C08; calculation C13; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 24
### Downside scenario

The downside path starts with mortgage rates staying elevated and builder demand softening further, so D.R. Horton slows takedowns of the lots it has under contract and seeks lower prices. The first operational break is closings moving beyond the usual three to eighteen months, with earnest money of 9.32% of remaining sales price the only stated protection and the company free to retain or refund it on cancellation depending on the contract, while development spending on projects already started continues. Revenue and gross profit fall against overhead of USD 154.4 million in fiscal 2025, operating cash flow turns negative as it did in fiscal 2024 and 2025 even when revenue grew, and inventory rises.

Basis: calculation C06; calculation C10; calculation C03; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-09-30_for-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15

On the sensitivities in the calculations, a 25% fall in EBITDA to USD 190.3 million would put total debt at 4.17x and net debt at 2.10x, and if a fiscal 2025-sized free cash outflow of USD 199.9 million recurred, net debt would reach USD 598.8 million, 3.15x the reduced EBITDA and 24.39% of total capital, still well below the issuer's 40% aim. Liquidity of USD 1,064.8 million would still cover the notes due March 2028 3.55x, and the borrowing base, which is set on real estate book value and unrestricted cash, and the unquantified covenants are the unknowns. Management has levers: cut land and development spending, as it did by USD 491.7 million, walk away from land purchase contracts with deposits of USD 33.7 million against USD 615.9 million of remaining price, trim overhead, sell tract land and use the equity program with USD 300.0 million reserved. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress before March 2028, but leverage would rise sharply and refinancing would be at a higher cost, so the scenario weakens the credit without breaking it. The observable triggers are listed in the monitoring register.
Basis: calculation C11; calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_for-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 24
### Overall credit view

Overall, Forestar presents an adequate business profile supported by modest leverage, USD 1,064.8 million of liquidity and contracted lots with its controlling shareholder, but credit quality is constrained by dependence on that shareholder for most revenue and by cash flow that follows inventory spending. Cash-flow durability appears adequate: EBITDA has stayed between USD 237.8 million and USD 281.4 million across three fiscal years and land spending is discretionary, but free cash flow was close to nil over those years. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on market access for the USD 300.0 million of notes due March 2028, the parent's continued purchases, and the borrowing base and covenants on the revolver. The primary downside path is a slower parent taking fewer lots at lower prices while development spending continues, which turns operating cash flow negative and raises net leverage. Further analysis would require cash interest paid, covenant levels and compliance certificates, the executed agreements with D.R. Horton, price by customer, results for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026 and peer data. Top risk: dependence on D.R. Horton's lot purchases.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C10; calculation C11; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
